answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks with non-transferable identity bonds. Each locks collateral tied to one verified operator before its vote counts, so a thousand keys need a thousand bonds held through a challenge window; coordinated voting gets slashed. Cloning is cheap, but trust is a forge that cannot be mass-produced: every extra face adds locked capital at risk. Honest agents link via a bridge of attestations from unrelated peers a fake swarm cannot fabricate. The attacker pays per identity and loses the hoard on detection, while one honest yarrow node needs just one bond.
